provenance.resolutionNote: Saving a quote draft is an internal product operation, not a legal act: same reasoning as every other shipped country file's own quote.save-draft: no Algerian text identified that would specifically govern this act (decree 05-468 and the CTCA only speak of the 'facture', never of a quote/devis).

Algeria is not an EU member state, so the eIDAS regulation (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014) other shipped country files cite for this exact rule does not apply here. The issue #558 research pass's scope was invoicing law (VAT, numbering, identifiers, corrections, retention, currency): it did not cover Algerian electronic-signature or electronic-writing law, so this stays unverified rather than guessed. What would settle it: an Algerian text on the legal admissibility of an electronic signature or an electronically sent commercial document.

Converting an accepted quote into an invoice is a product convenience; no Algerian text identified imposes or forbids this precise mechanism. The only legal constraint bears on the resulting invoice itself (see invoice.save-draft/invoice.send below), never on this prior act of conversion from a quote.

Requesting a deposit on a quote, in the form of a draft deposit invoice, is a product convenience of the same nature as 'convert-to-invoice' above; no Algerian text identified governs this precise mechanism. Decree 05-468 art. 3 lists 'mode de paiement et date de reglement de la facture' among an invoice's mandatory mentions, but that bears on the resulting deposit invoice once issued, never on this prior act of requesting it from a quote still in draft.

Generating a billing schedule from an accepted quote (several draft invoices, one per installment) is a product convenience of the same nature as 'request-deposit' above; no Algerian text identified governs this precise mechanism. The only legal constraint bears on the invoices that will result once issued (see invoice.save-draft/invoice.send below), never on this prior act of generation from a quote still in draft.
Duplicating a quote into a new draft is a pure product convenience; no Algerian text identified governs it.

Generating an unauthenticated public link to a quote's PDF is a product convenience: a quote is not even a 'facture' within the meaning of decree 05-468. No Algerian text identified that would specifically govern the sharing of a link to a document already communicated to its recipient.

Asking a client to electronically sign a quote (link + OTP code by email: signatures/signatures.service.ts) is a product convenience: a quote is not a 'facture' within the meaning of decree 05-468, and signing a quote is not, on the evidence gathered so far, a legally regulated act in Algeria. The issue #558 research pass did not cover Algerian electronic-signature law (see quote.send above): this stays unverified for the same reason.

No legal research was performed for this entry: this action records an issuer-side fact only (who marked a sent quote accepted, when, and by what means) and changes no fiscal fact and produces no document a third party ever receives, the same kind of internal record quote.duplicate above already sits on. What would settle it: an Algerian text conditioning the evidentiary value of a quote's acceptance on the channel through which it was obtained: not researched here.

provenance.sourceText: La facture doit etre lisible et ne comprendre aucune tache, rature ou surcharge. La facture est reputee reguliere lorsqu'elle est extraite d'un carnet a souches denomme facturier quelle que soit sa forme ou etablie sous la forme dematerialisee a travers le recours a un procede informatique. Le facturier est un carnet a souches comprenant une serie ininterrompue et chronologique de factures sur lesquelles devront figurer, lors de la realisation de la transaction, les mentions definies au niveau des articles 3 et 4 ci-dessus. Un facturier ne peut etre entame sans que le precedent ne soit totalement epuise. La facture regulierement annulee doit faire l'objet d'une mention << facture annulee >> inscrite clairement en diagonale.

rules.notes: Decret executif n. 05-468 du 10 decembre 2005, art. 10: full article, read and quoted verbatim by the issue #558 research pass (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md, section 3 and section 4). The text forbids any erasure, correction mark, or overwrite ('aucune tache, rature ou surcharge') on an issued invoice, and provides exactly one way to undo one: cancelling it outright with a diagonal 'facture annulee' mention, never silently rewriting it. This settles the same fact `statuses: ["draft"]` applies for every other shipped country file: an already-issued invoice is never rewritten through a fresh draft save, only ever explicitly cancelled.

provenance.sourceText: La facture est reputee reguliere lorsqu'elle est extraite d'un carnet a souches denomme facturier quelle que soit sa forme ou etablie sous la forme dematerialisee a travers le recours a un procede informatique.

rules.notes: Decret executif n. 05-468, art. 10 (same article as invoice.save-draft above, different clause): the decree explicitly recognizes a dematerialized invoice ('etablie sous la forme dematerialisee a travers le recours a un procede informatique') as a regular invoice, alongside a paper carnet a souches. This authorizes issuing and sending an Algerian invoice electronically. NUANCE NOT MODELED HERE: the wet stamp and signature requirement of the decree's own art. 4 admits an exception for 'transmission telematique' per the research pass's own summary (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md section 2), but that pass's own Sources section does not carry a verbatim quote of art. 4 or art. 11, only a paraphrase, so this rule does not cite either article directly and does not model the stamp/signature exception itself; what would settle it is reading decree 05-468 art. 4 and art. 11 directly and quoting them verbatim.

provenance.resolutionNote: SOURCED ABSENCE, same corpus as invoice.duplicate below: decret executif n. 05-468 (see invoice.send above) names no distinct "validate" act separate from the invoice's own issuance (numbering, locking). `transports/channel-policy/data/dz.json` carries no `"mandated"` channel fact for Algeria - `resolveActiveInvoiceMandate` (actions/invoice-actions.ts's "validate" handler, issue #581) therefore never routes an Algerian invoice through a real send here: this rule is a plain unblock, with no further branching for the acting mechanism to decide at runtime, unlike France's own. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS FURTHER: the same decree 05-468 art. 4/art. 11 reading invoice.send's own note already names as unresolved for the stamp/signature exception - no new research gap specific to this action.
Duplicating an invoice into a new DRAFT (never a resend of the original issued document) is a product convenience; no Algerian text identified governs it.

Recording that an invoice was paid is an internal bookkeeping record, not itself a legal act under decree 05-468 or the CTCA as read by the issue #558 research pass. Decree 05-468 art. 3 requires the invoice to STATE 'mode de paiement et date de reglement' at issuance, but that bears on the invoice's own content, not on this separate, later record.

No structured electronic invoice format (e.g. an EN 16931 syntax) is mandated for Algeria: see transports/channel-policy/data/dz.json's own notes: no e-invoicing obligation was found in any primary source reached by the issue #558 research pass. Whether offering a structured export at all is meaningful for Algeria is therefore itself unverified, kept allowed (a product convenience, never a legal claim) rather than removed.

Not implemented by this branch for any country (see actions/invoice-actions.ts's own header: this action is declared on the descriptor and deliberately not registered): this entry documents the same 'no Algerian text identified' posture every other shipped country file already holds for it, kept consistent rather than special-cased.

Generating an unauthenticated public link to an issued invoice's PDF is a product convenience; no Algerian text identified that would specifically govern the sharing of a link to a document already delivered to its recipient.

Decree 05-468 defines no 'facture d'avoir'/credit-note instrument at all (see correction-routes/data/dz.json's own CREDIT_NOTE route): whether Algerian law has anything to say about drafting one is therefore itself unresolved, not merely this specific act.

Same reasoning as credit-note.save-draft above: no Algerian legal basis for a credit note as a distinct instrument was identified by the issue #558 research pass, so sending one is kept allowed as a product convenience without a legal claim behind it.
Same reasoning as credit-note.save-draft above.
No structured electronic format is mandated for Algeria (see invoice.download-xml above); kept allowed as a product convenience.
An expense record is this company's own internal bookkeeping of what it spent, never a document issued to or received from anyone else; no Algerian text identified governs it.
Same reasoning as expense.save-draft above.

Recording that this company received a supplier's own invoice is this company's own internal record of a document a SUPPLIER issued under whatever rules govern the supplier's own country; no Algerian text identified specifically governs the act of recording receipt itself.
Same reasoning as received-invoice.receive above.
Same reasoning as received-invoice.receive above.
Same reasoning as invoice.record-payment above, applied to a received (supplier) invoice instead.
Same reasoning as received-invoice.receive above.
A purchase order is a document this company sends to its own supplier; it is not a 'facture' within the meaning of decree 05-468, and no Algerian text identified governs it.
Same reasoning as quote.send above: the issue #558 research pass did not cover Algerian electronic-signature or electronic-writing law, so this stays unverified rather than guessed.
A purchase order is not a 'facture'; no Algerian text identified governs cancelling one.
A goods receipt is an internal record of what arrived; it is never sent to a tax authority or a buyer, and no Algerian text identified governs it.
Same reasoning as goods-receipt.save-draft above.
Same reasoning as goods-receipt.save-draft above.

provenance.sourceText: Toute facturation ou vente de biens et services sur le territoire douanier national s'effectue en dinars algeriens sauf cas prevus par la reglementation en vigueur.

domesticInvoiceCurrency.notes: Reglement de la Banque d'Algerie n. 07-01 du 3 fevrier 2007 relatif aux regles applicables aux transactions courantes avec l'etranger et aux comptes devises, art. 5: read directly and quoted verbatim by the issue #558 research pass (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md, section 7), verified not amended by any later Banque d'Algerie regulation up to and including reglement n. 26-02 du 23 juillet 2026. Binds a DOMESTIC Algerian sale ('sur le territoire douanier national'); export invoicing in a foreign currency is consistent with this same regulation's own repatriation-of-proceeds mechanism (art. 61) but no sentence explicitly authorizes it in so many words: a deduction, not a quoted rule, so this fact only ever fires for a seller and buyer BOTH established in Algeria (see the domestic-currency preflight's own header for how 'domestic' is decided, mirroring transports/channel-policy/mandate.ts's own isDomestic).

constraints.summary: Algerian law requires an uninterrupted, chronological series of invoices (a carnet a souches, or its dematerialized equivalent): a new booklet cannot be opened before the previous one is fully used. It constrains continuity, not a specific character set or length.

provenance.sourceText: Le facturier est un carnet a souches comprenant une serie ininterrompue et chronologique de factures sur lesquelles devront figurer, lors de la realisation de la transaction, les mentions definies au niveau des articles 3 et 4 ci-dessus. Un facturier ne peut etre entame sans que le precedent ne soit totalement epuise.

constraints.notes: Decret executif n. 05-468, art. 10: same article as invoice.save-draft/invoice.send above, read and quoted verbatim by the issue #558 research pass. No length or character-set limit is stated anywhere in the decree; the constraint is continuity alone.

formats.unconstrained: A quote is not a 'facture' within the meaning of decree 05-468 or loi n. 04-02; no Algerian text read by the issue #558 research pass constrains the number of a quote.
formats.rationale: Unchanged from the product's previous shared default, so every company already running a quote series keeps reading the same shape.

resetProvenance.resolutionNote: Issue #515: no Algerian text governs the numbering of a quote at all (see this format's own "unconstrained" statement above): there is no numbering-continuity obligation to read a yearly-restart permission FROM. Stays the safe default: one continuous counter, {year} printing only the moment of issuance.

formats.rationale: Unchanged from the product's previous shared default, so a company already running it keeps it as it is. Decree 05-468 limits no character and no length, only continuity.

resetProvenance.sourceText: Le facturier est un carnet a souches comprenant une serie ininterrompue et chronologique de factures [...] Un facturier ne peut etre entame sans que le precedent ne soit totalement epuise.

formats.notes: Decret executif n. 05-468, art. 10 (same quote as the constraint above). This is stronger than mere silence: the text requires an UNINTERRUPTED series and explicitly forbids starting a new booklet before the previous one is exhausted: a yearly restart to 1 would break that continuity outright, so `reset: "never"` is sourced to an affirmative reading of the text, not only to the absence of a permission (contrast this format's own siblings below, each `unverified` for lack of any text at all).

formats.unconstrained: No Algerian text establishes a credit note as a distinct legal instrument at all (see correction-routes/data/dz.json's own CREDIT_NOTE route, unverified): there is nothing to read a numbering rule FROM.
formats.rationale: The same short form as the other countries, so a company working across them reads one convention, in a series of its own, distinct from the invoice series.

resetProvenance.resolutionNote: Issue #515: no credit-note instrument is established in Algerian law at all (see this format's own "unconstrained" statement above), so there is nothing to read a yearly-restart permission from either. Stays the safe default.

runningSeries.summary: A series this company already started is kept as it is: Algerian law asks for an uninterrupted, chronological series, and switching a running series to another format is never required by it.

provenance.sourceText: Le facturier est un carnet a souches comprenant une serie ininterrompue et chronologique de factures [...] Un facturier ne peut etre entame sans que le precedent ne soit totalement epuise.

runningSeries.onViolation: No Algerian constraint limits the characters or the length of the number, so a running series can only fall back when its own pattern cannot be rendered at all. The country format then applies from the next number; the counter is not reset and no number is reused: reusing one, or leaving a gap, would itself break the required uninterrupted series.

notes: Algeria (DZ), issue #558, transcribed 2026-09-30 from RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md. Document-action rules: two of thirty-three sourced 'legal' (invoice.save-draft, invoice.send, both from decree 05-468 art. 10, read and quoted in full), the other thirty-one honestly 'unverified': this action-policy question was explicitly out of scope for the issue #558 research pass itself ('country-policy/data/dz.json (actions autorisees): Pas recherche du tout dans cette passe: a faire', RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md's own effort estimate), and this file does not pretend otherwise. `domesticInvoiceCurrency` (a new, cross-country schema field added by this same PR at the owner's explicit request) sources Algeria's DZD-only domestic invoicing obligation to the Banque d'Algerie's own currency regulation. `numberFormats` sources the invoice's own continuity requirement to decree 05-468 art. 10; every other document type is honestly unconstrained, matching this product's own convention for a type no Algerian text was found to govern.
